## Fourth-order, cell-consistent face density reference (`SNAP_WB_REF4`) {#sec-ch05-wbref4}

### Summary

The kernel's face density is not the face value of its own cell density, so the solver's face density carries
the offset @eq-ch05-refkernel-offset. That offset enters the $x_1$ mass flux at linear order and, through it, the
gravity work. The switch removes it with one operator: it replaces the face density by the face value of the
kernel's own cell density, taken from the quartic through the primitive of that cell field, so that face and cell
are consistent by construction. Nothing else is replaced. The cell density reference, the cell pressure and the
face pressures, and so the rest state, are the kernel's on any grid.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Makes the reference face density the face value of the kernel's own cell density, @eq-ch05-wbref4-face.

**Data.** Reads $\rho_{\mathrm{ref}}$ and $p_{\mathrm{sf}}$ of the kernel; replaces $\rho_{\mathrm{sf}}$ only.

**Placement.** Inside `HydroImpl::_hydro_ref_x1`: the resolution flag right after the kernel, the faces after the seam exchange.

**Activation.** Environment variable `SNAP_WB_REF4` (or `SNAP_X1_CENTROID_EXACT`), default off; needs $n_g\ge3$.

**Guarantee / limits.** $\eta_{\rho,f}=O(\Delta x_1^4)$ where no guard fires; $\rho_{\mathrm{ref}}$, $p_{\mathrm{sf}}$ and so the rest balance are unchanged.

**Evidence.** The Tests layer below, @tbl-ch05-wbref4-tests.
:::

Local symbols: $\Pi$ [kg m$^{-2}$] the primitive of the cell reference
density; $i_0$ the first cell of a stencil window, $l$ the cell offset in it and $l_{\mathrm f}$ the face offset; $\ell_{l_{\mathrm f}}$
the Lagrange basis polynomial of face $i_0+l_{\mathrm f}$; $\tilde p$ [Pa] the cubic through four face pressures; $\zeta$ a
Gauss-Legendre node; $n_{\mathrm{poly}}$ the polytropic index and $\mathcal S_i$ [J kg$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$ s$^{-1}$] the entropy
tendency of cell $i$, both in the order test. $\vartheta$[^rg-3739b5b2fec3], $\lambda_w$[^rg-cf66429c8e8b], $\chi$, $\eta_{\rho,f}$, $\mathcal W$, $\Delta x_1$, $n_g$ and $\epsilon_{\mathrm m}$ are defined in @sec-appa
or @sec-ch05-refkernel.

Guards keep the kernel's face value wherever the new one would leave the range of its two neighbouring cells or
the column is under-resolved, and the face part runs after the seam exchange of @sec-ch05-seam. With the corrected-PE[^rg-36523dc32e4e] face
work of @sec-ch06 on (its default with `gravity-work: face`), the one-step spurious stratification of a neutral column
converges at about fourth order with the switch and second order without it.

*Aliases.* "Leg W" in the centroid derivation note; `SNAPY_WB_REF_EXACT` in the specification.[^ch05-wb4-alias]

[^ch05-wb4-alias]: `docs/derivations/x1-centroid-spherical.md`; `sources/gw__NEXTPR_spec_wbref_exact.md`.

### Derivation

Notation as in @sec-ch05-refkernel; indices are cell indices and $\chi_i=\overline\rho_i/\overline p_i$. The derivation is
that of the derivation note,[^ch05-wb4-note] re-written here and checked by `[C3]`, `[C7]`, `[C8]`, `[C14]`.

[^ch05-wb4-note]: `docs/derivations/wb-ref4.md@919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274` §§2-7.

#### Why only the face value

$\eta_{\rho,f}=\rho_{\mathrm{sf},f}-\mathcal W[\rho_{\mathrm{ref}}]_f$ of @eq-ch05-refkernel-offset is the offset
between the kernel's face density and the face value of the kernel's own cell density. What the solver puts on the face is
$\mathcal W[\overline\rho-\rho_{\mathrm{ref}}]_f+\rho_{\mathrm{sf},f}=\mathcal W[\overline\rho]_f+\eta_{\rho,f}$, by
linearity of the reconstruction. So the face density is a consistent high-order face value exactly when
$\rho_{\mathrm{sf}}$ is the face value of the cell field $\rho_{\mathrm{ref}}$, **whatever the accuracy of
$\rho_{\mathrm{ref}}$ itself**: a bias shared by the cell reference and its face value is subtracted and added back
and cannot reach the flux. One operator therefore closes the offset, and the switch replaces nothing else. The
cell density reference stays the kernel's $p_{\mathrm{ref}}\chi^{s}$ of @eq-ch05-refkernel-dens, and so does
every pressure.

#### Face density

$$
\begin{aligned}
\rho_{\mathrm{sf},f} &= \partial_1 \Pi(x_{1,f}), \\
\Pi(x_{1,i_0+l_{\mathrm f}}) &= \sum_{l<l_{\mathrm f}}\rho_{\mathrm{ref},i_0+l}\,\Delta x_{1,i_0+l},
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch05-wbref4-face}

with $\Pi$ the quartic through the primitive at the five faces $l_{\mathrm f}=0..4$ (four cells), window $i_0=f-2$ kept inside the owned cells at a
clamped wall, physical spacing. On a uniform grid of width $\Delta x_1$, $\Pi$ takes the values $0,\ \Delta x_1\rho_{\mathrm{ref},i_0},\ \Delta x_1(\rho_{\mathrm{ref},i_0}+\rho_{\mathrm{ref},i_0+1}),\dots$
at the faces $l_{\mathrm f}=0..4$; writing $\Pi$ in the Lagrange basis $\ell_{l_{\mathrm f}}$ of those five faces and differentiating,
$\rho_{\mathrm{sf},i_0+l_{\mathrm f}}=\partial_1\Pi(x_{1,i_0+l_{\mathrm f}})=\sum_{l=0}^{3}\rho_{\mathrm{ref},i_0+l}\,\Delta x_1\sum_{l'_{\mathrm f}>l}\partial_1\ell_{l'_{\mathrm f}}(x_{1,i_0+l_{\mathrm f}})$, which on
$\rho_{\mathrm{ref},i_0..i_0+3}$ is $(25,-23,13,-3)/12$ at $l_{\mathrm f}=0$ (the wall face), $(3,13,-5,1)/12$ at $l_{\mathrm f}=1$ (the next) and
$(-1,7,7,-1)/12$ at $l_{\mathrm f}=2$ (the interior face, window $i_0=f-2$) (`[C8]`). The face is exact for cubic
point profiles on any grid, so $\eta_{\rho,f}=\rho_{\mathrm{sf}}-\mathcal W[\rho_{\mathrm{ref}}]=O(\Delta x_1^4)$ (`[C14]`:
mid-column offset $3.22\times10^{-12}$, $5.18\times10^{-14}$, $6.91\times10^{-16}$ relative at $n_1$ = 32, 64, 128, orders
5.96 and 6.23, against order 2.00 for the kernel; at $n_1=256$ it is at round-off level, $1.38\times10^{-16}$ in this run, so
that level measures round-off, not truncation). @eq-ch05-wbref4-face is built as the weights `awt`
({{< code src/hydro/wb_ref4.cpp wb_ref4_stencils >}})
and applied by `wb_ref4_faces`
({{< code src/hydro/wb_ref4.cpp wb_ref4_faces >}}).

#### Cell pressure and cell density

The switch changes no cell value, on any grid: `wb_ref4_faces` writes only $\rho_{\mathrm{sf}}$
({{< code src/hydro/wb_ref4.cpp wb_ref4_faces >}}), and `wb_ref4_flag` reads the scan pressures and returns a
boolean ({{< code src/hydro/wb_ref4.cpp wb_ref4_flag >}}). On a uniform grid the cell pressure is the six-face
pressure of @eq-ch05-refkernel-pref; on a keyed stretched $x_1$ it is the six-face average built from the widths,
@eq-ch05-refkernel-stretched, of sixth order. The rest state is therefore the kernel's with the switch on or off,
and `balance_column` does not call the switch (@sec-ch05-balcol). The stencils of the face part use the face
positions (physical spacing), so they apply to a stretched $x_1$ as built.

#### Guards and rest balance

A face whose new value lies outside the range of its two neighbouring cell references keeps the kernel's face,
with relative margin $10^{-10}$. A cell with $\lvert\ln(p_{\mathrm{sf},i-1/2}/p_{\mathrm{sf},i+1/2})\rvert>0.5$,
fewer than two cells per pressure scale height, is flagged, the flag is dilated by two cells, and a face with a
flagged cell on either side keeps the kernel's value; ghosts past a clamped wall do not count. The flag reads
$p_{\mathrm{sf}}$ at most three cells away, which is why $n_g\ge3$ is required: then both sides of an $x_1$ seam
compute the same flag. The threshold, dilation and margin are design choices, not derived. Since neither
$p_{\mathrm{sf}}$ nor $p_{\mathrm{ref}}$ nor $\rho_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is changed, the rest state
@eq-ch05-wbx1-rest is the kernel's.

*Why the two sides of an $x_1$ seam agree.* Three steps.

1. *The flag is local.* `wb_ref4_flag` reads only the block's own scan pressures, so it needs no exchange; it is
   built right after the kernel ({{< code src/hydro/wb_ref4.cpp wb_ref4_flag >}}).
2. *The face part reads only exchanged cells.* `wb_ref4_faces` runs after the seam exchange of
   $(p_{\mathrm{ref}},\rho_{\mathrm{ref}})$, and its four-cell window at an interior face reaches two cells past the
   face, inside $n_g\ge2$. The flag of a cell is dilated by two cells (`max_pool1d` of width 5), so a face next to a
   seam depends on scan pressures up to three cells away; with $n_g\ge3$ both blocks hold them, which is the setup
   check.
3. *The guard does not flip on round-off.* `in_range` widens each bound by `kMargin` $=10^{-10}$ relative, far above
   the round-off of the next paragraph, so a split column and one block take the same branch on a flat profile,
   where the two bounds coincide.

*Round-off.* The face weights are computed in double by `lagrange_deriv`, so they carry a rounding of their own
that is not bounded here; their four-term sum adds at most $4\epsilon_{\mathrm m}\sum_l\lvert a_l\rvert\max\rho_{\mathrm{ref}}
=\tfrac{16}{3}\epsilon_{\mathrm m}\max\rho_{\mathrm{ref}}$ in the interior, with $\sum_l\lvert a_l\rvert=16/12$ for the
weights $a_l=(-1,7,7,-1)/12$. The $n_1=256$ level of `[C14]`, at round-off level, lies inside it.

*Exact and truncated.* Exact: the face weights for cubics. $O(\Delta x_1^4)$: $\eta_{\rho,f}$ in the interior. At the
three faces next to a wall the note gives $O(\Delta x_1^3)$ (the anchor constant through the even ghosts); not
re-checked here. The cell reference keeps the kernel's second-order bias, which @eq-ch05-refkernel-dens carries and
which cancels out of the face value by the argument above.

### Numerical method

The stencil is shown in @fig-ch05-wbref4-stencils. The stencils and weights are built once per block, on the CPU in double
precision, and cached until device or dtype changes; application is a gather and a weighted sum on the block's device.
The resolution flag is built right after the kernel in `_hydro_ref_x1`; the face part runs after the seam ghost-row
exchange, so a column split along $x_1$ gets the same faces as one block. A block with a clamped wall and fewer than
four owned cells keeps the kernel's reference.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch05-wbref4-stencils
#| fig-cap: "The `SNAP_WB_REF4` face stencil at a bottom wall (thick black line), $x_1$ to the right. The face density at the wall face comes from the quartic primitive over the four owned cells next to the wall (orange triangles at the five faces, sky-blue circles at the cell references the weights read); the window is kept inside the owned cells there, so the hatched ghosts are never read. Interior faces use the centred weights $(-1, 7, 7, -1)/12$."
#| fig-alt: "A row of cells beside a wall with hatched ghosts, triangles marking five faces and circles marking four cell values, under a bracket of four cells."
#| echo: false
from snapy_report.ch05.figures.fig_wbref4_stencils import make_fig
make_fig()
```

**The oracle and the measured order.** The test drives a neutral polytrope ($\gamma=5/3$, $g=n_{\mathrm{poly}}+1$ with
the polytropic index $n_{\mathrm{poly}}=1/(\gamma-1)$, $T_0=1+L_z-z$) seeded with a divergence-free overturning mode of amplitude $10^{-4}$, takes one RK3[^rg-5ce8343548de]
step, and measures $N^2_{\mathrm{eff}}=\tfrac g\gamma\sum_i(-\mathcal S_i)v_{1,i}/\sum_iv_{1,i}^2$ from the entropy tendency $\mathcal S_i$ of
the mode minus that of the rest state. For this column the exact cell-average tendencies vanish at linear order, so every
$N^2_{\mathrm{eff}}$ is scheme error. @fig-ch05-wbref4-order shows the four arms at the pin.[^ch05-wb4-fig]

[^ch05-wb4-fig]: Data `src/snapy_report/ch05/data/wb_ref4_order.json`, from `python tests/test_wb_ref4_order.py` (from the
    build's `tests` directory, `PYTHONPATH` set to this build's Python package) against a CPU Release source build of snapy@68f4e066974ede87e4379285c4fba895b970b7f1 (Python 3.11.13, torch 2.10.0, kintera 2.6.6, GCC 11.5.0), 2026-11-08, double, 1 rank; the
    `SNAP_GRAVITY_WORK_RADIAL_EXACT=0` arms from a second run with that variable set. The test sets

### Code

**A minimal input.** The switch is an environment variable, not a YAML key. A deck it acts on needs gravity along
$x_1$, three ghost cells and, for the wall stencils, the wall clamp:

```yaml
geometry:
  type: cartesian
  bounds: {x1min: 0., x1max: 1.e4}
  cells: {nx1: 64, nghost: 3}   # three ghost cells: the setup check below
dynamics:
  wb-wall-clamp: true           # the default; the wall stencils use owned cells only
forcing:
  const-gravity: {grav1: -9.8}
```

With these keys in a copy of `straka_single.yaml`, saved as `deck.yaml` in `build/bin` of a build at the pin
([Install and run](#sec-preface-install)), run

```bash
SNAP_WB_REF4=1 ./straka.release deck.yaml
```

A PyPI release of snapy has no such switch and ignores the variable without a message.

**What it refuses, and why.** Setup refuses $n_g<3$ with gravity on
({{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::reset >}}), because the flag of step 3 above would then read
cells a block does not hold, and the two sides of a seam could disagree. Values of `SNAP_WB_REF4` other than empty,
`0`, `false`, `off` or `no` (any case) turn it on. A block with a clamped wall and fewer than four owned cells, or with
fewer than five cells in all, is not refused: its stencils are marked unusable
({{< code src/hydro/wb_ref4.cpp wb_ref4_stencils >}}) and it keeps the kernel's reference.

**The lines that implement @eq-ch05-wbref4-face.** From `wb_ref4_flag` and `wb_ref4_faces`:

```cpp
auto bad = ((psf_lo / psf_hi).log().abs() > kMaxLogDrop) & st.counted;
return torch::max_pool1d(bad.to(psf_lo.dtype()).reshape({-1, 1, st.nc1}), 5,
                         1, 2).reshape(sizes) > 0.;
...
auto face = apply(dref, st.aidx, st.awt);
auto ok = in_range(face, torch::minimum(dl, dr), torch::maximum(dl, dr)) &
          ~flag.narrow(-1, st.is - 1, nf) & ~flag.narrow(-1, st.is, nf);
d.copy_(torch::where(ok, face, d));
```

`bad` is the under-resolution test and `max_pool1d` the two-cell dilation, together the flag
({{< code src/hydro/wb_ref4.cpp wb_ref4_flag >}}). `face` is $\partial_1\Pi(x_{1,f})$ of @eq-ch05-wbref4-face with
the weights `awt`, read from the kernel's cell reference `dref`, which is never written; `ok` is the range guard
and the flag of the two cells beside the face, and where it fails the kernel's $\rho_{\mathrm{sf}}$ (`d`) stays
({{< code src/hydro/wb_ref4.cpp wb_ref4_faces >}}).

|--------|----------|----------|------|
| the switch, implied by the centroid switch | {{< code src/hydro/wb_ref4.cpp wb_ref4_enabled >}} | `wb_ref4_enabled` | `SNAP_WB_REF4` |
| margin and resolution threshold | {{< code src/hydro/wb_ref4.cpp kMaxLogDrop >}} | `kMaxLogDrop`, `kMargin` | |
| stencils and weights | {{< code src/hydro/wb_ref4.cpp wb_ref4_stencils >}} | `wb_ref4_stencils` | |
| resolution flag | {{< code src/hydro/wb_ref4.cpp wb_ref4_flag >}} | `wb_ref4_flag` | |
| face part | {{< code src/hydro/wb_ref4.cpp wb_ref4_faces >}} | `wb_ref4_faces` | |
| ghost-depth check | {{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::reset >}} | `wb_ref4_enabled` | $n_g\ge3$ |
| calls around the seam exchange | {{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::_hydro_ref_x1 >}} | `wb_ref4_flag` | |

: Code map of `SNAP_WB_REF4`. {#tbl-ch05-wbref4-code}

1. `wb_ref4_enabled` reads the environment once; values other than empty, `0`, `false`, `off`, `no` turn it on, and
   `SNAP_X1_CENTROID_EXACT` turns it on too
   ({{< code src/hydro/wb_ref4.cpp wb_ref4_enabled >}}).
2. At setup, with gravity on, $n_g<3$ fails the `TORCH_CHECK` that names `wb_ref4_enabled`
   ({{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::reset >}}).
3. In `_hydro_ref_x1` the stencils are built once per block from the face positions and `wb_ref4_flag` returns
   the resolution flag; the cell reference is left as the kernel built it
   ({{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::_hydro_ref_x1 >}}).
4. After the seam exchange `wb_ref4_faces` replaces $\rho_{\mathrm{sf}}$
   ({{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::_hydro_ref_x1 >}}).

The only user-facing error is the ghost-depth check of step 2.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
`SNAP_WB_REF4` needs `nghost` $\ge3$. It is read once per process, so every block of a run makes the same choice.
:::

1. **Thresholds not derived.** The $0.5$ resolution threshold, the two-cell dilation and the $10^{-10}$ margin are
   design choices.[^ch05-wb4-thr]
2. **Untested.** The order of the density reference on a stretched $x_1$ (the stretched test only builds and steps
   a deck with the switch), multi-species columns, and seams across more than two ranks.
3. **Resolution of the order test.** The test grid is $n_1$ = 32/64/128 against 64/128/256 in the note's table, and the
   threshold `ORDER_ON` 2.75 does not distinguish the fourth order measured at the pin from the third order of the
   note; the test still separates on from off.
4. **Names.** The specification calls the switch `SNAPY_WB_REF_EXACT`; the code reads `SNAP_WB_REF4`.
5. **Untested combinations.** See the switch coverage matrix, @sec-ch12-matrix.
